title: Clinical Laboratory Scientist, Lab AdminGeneral, Mid County - Full time

cond_0001.intro: This position performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures including specimen processing and handling, testing of patient specimens, calculating, and reporting of results, performance of quality control procedures, operation and maintenance of instruments and equipment, assisting in the development of new procedures and protocols, may perform phlebotomy and other patient-oriented tasks, and may perform other related duties as requested or directed.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Participates in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks)
OR
Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current. New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS.
OR
Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
OR
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).

OR
Education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology

cond_0027.intro: This position performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures including specimen processing and handling, testing of patient specimens, calculating, and reporting of results, performance of quality control procedures, operation and maintenance of instruments and equipment, assisting in the development of new procedures and protocols, may perform phlebotomy and other patient-oriented tasks, and may perform other related duties as requested or directed.
cond_0027.responsibilities:
Works within the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies framework: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Carries out all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section assigned, with attention to age- or sex-specific values.
Coordinates with Bio-med staff to maintain and troubleshoot laboratory instrumentation and equipment, making minor repairs as needed.
Cross-trains with other laboratory sections as needed to support team coverage.
Works with the team to ensure the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures in coordination with relevant staff.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System in collaboration with the broader lab team.
Shares notification and documentation of critical laboratory values with appropriate personnel.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution, always mindful of minimal pediatric specimen volumes when required.
Participates alongside colleagues in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to support assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Works with care teams to adapt patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age-specific, and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Completes all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follows all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0027.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution, or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks)
OR
Education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, it must be maintained and kept current. New Graduates who are Board Certified or eligible must complete Board Certification within 1 year of hire ([Location masked] excluded)
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS
OR
Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, including a clinical rotation through Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years
OR
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II)

cond_0184.responsibilities: Meets expectations of the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders. Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values. Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed. Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed. Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed. Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures. Utilizes the Laboratory Information System. Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained. Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required). Participates in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols. Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department. Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age specific and other developmental needs of each patient served. Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0184.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks), OR education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current. New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS.
Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
cond_0184.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0184.values: We value work that supports people well and reflects genuine care in how it is done. We believe responsibility and respect matter as much as the end result.

Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks), OR education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current. New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS.
Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).

cond_0225.responsibilities:
Works within the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies framework: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Carries out all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section assigned, with attention to age- or sex-specific values.
Coordinates with Bio-med staff to maintain and troubleshoot laboratory instrumentation and equipment, making minor repairs as needed.
Cross-trains with other laboratory sections as needed to support team coverage.
Works with the team to ensure the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures in coordination with relevant staff.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System in collaboration with the broader lab team.
Shares notification and documentation of critical laboratory values with appropriate personnel.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution, always mindful of minimal pediatric specimen volumes when required.
Participates alongside colleagues in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to support assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Works with care teams to adapt patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age-specific, and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Completes all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follows all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.

cond_0259.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values.

Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.

cond_0259.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution, or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks); OR education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, it must be maintained and kept current. New Graduates who are Board Certified or eligible must complete Board Certification within 1 year of hire ([Location masked] excluded).

One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS; OR two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, including a clinical rotation through Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).

Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution, or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks)
OR
Education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, it must be maintained and kept current. New Graduates who are Board Certified or eligible must complete Board Certification within 1 year of hire ([Location masked] excluded)
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS
OR
Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, including a clinical rotation through Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years
OR
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II)

Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values. Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed. Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed. Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed. Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department. Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age specific and other developmental needs of each patient served. Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0352.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks)
OR
Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.

5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).

Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks)
OR
Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current. New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS.
OR
Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
OR
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).

cond_0362.intro: This position performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures including specimen processing and handling, testing of patient specimens, calculating, and reporting of results, performance of quality control procedures, operation and maintenance of instruments and equipment, assisting in the development of new procedures and protocols, may perform phlebotomy and other patient-oriented tasks, and may perform other related duties as requested or directed.
cond_0362.responsibilities: Meets expectations of the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders. Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values. Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed. Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed. Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed. Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures. Utilizes the Laboratory Information System. Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained. Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required). Participates in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols. Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department. Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age specific and other developmental needs of each patient served. Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures. Performs other duties as assigned.

cond_0399.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.

Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0399.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution, or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks); or education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a relevant science or medical technology field — equivalent practical experience is considered.
Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS, or willingness to obtain. If certification with an expiration date is held, it must be maintained and kept current. Around one year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS or other organizations approved by HHS; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Around two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, ideally including a clinical rotation through Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
Around five years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (please note: MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).

cond_0440.intro: This position performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures including specimen processing and handling, testing of patient specimens, calculating, and reporting of results, performance of quality control procedures, operation and maintenance of instruments and equipment, assisting in the development of new procedures and protocols, may perform phlebotomy and other patient-oriented tasks, and may perform other related duties as requested or directed.
cond_0440.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Executes all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Ensures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Directs use of the Laboratory Information System.
Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Leads participation in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0440.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks), OR education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS. If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current. New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS.
Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
5 Years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).

cond_0534.responsibilities: Meets expectations of the applicable [Company name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders. Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about age or sex specific values. Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed. Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed. Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed. Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures. Utilizes the Laboratory Information System. Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained. Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required). Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department. Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, age specific and other developmental needs of each patient served. Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0534.requirements:
A Bachelor's degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution, or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks), or equivalent practical experience.
OR
Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Around one year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS.
OR
Around two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which should include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years.
OR
Around 5 years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
Candidates should have, or be working toward, Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS.
